reasoning: The proposed change is partly a relabel and partly diagnosed in the wrong direction. Its useful part is 'keep the working pace of the line before'. That is supported, because the failed close ran about three times faster than the close that passed in take 3. The stated cause is 'a fall-off in pitch or slowing at the end', and the evidence contradicts it. Take 3 had the same fall-to-the-end and lowest-energy direction and passed this phrase. Take 4 shows compression, not slowing. Telling the reader 'no slowing at the end' could shorten the close further. 'Level, no slowing, no upturn' is also close to take 3's overall pacing text, which belonged to an earlier attempt, so this mechanism partly brings back old direction under a new id. A valid replacement states the supported cause, a close compressed and clipped at the end of the take, and uses the duration lever explicitly. Line 9's energy should ask for the close at the same tempo and length as line 8, as a complete phrase. The last word should be finished at normal length before the read ends. 'Lowest energy', 'low through the last word' and 'falls to the end' should be removed from lines 7 to 9, which the proposal already does correctly. Keep 'no upturn'. Add no pronunciation notes and no 'whole', 'unslurred' or short-i wording. That would bring back stress-phrase-articulation. The scope stays narrow: vo_direction.json only, two tts_calls, and the spoken script, claims, board, sources and renderer unchanged. The fresh soundcheck and the pinned whisper alignment remain the real test.
